rationale: As a 5/20 contact sheet, the set is still too small and too internally repetitive to read as a portfolio of distinct museum spatial families. Only four visible families are legible, with stepped box/slab and curved bar types each repeating as near-duplicates, giving a dominant family share of roughly 40% and no strong evidence yet of the required breadth. The set does show some progress toward a public-sequence language, but the variation remains mostly silhouette-level rather than a robust set of museum mass/section/threshold ideas. For a passing 20-option portfolio, the next batch must expand decisively into courtyard, carve-void, split-wing, bridge, cross-mass, and lift-based types with clear access/threshold relations and controlled daylight courts.

repeated_family_groups.shared_language: stepped box/slab family with frontage notch and recursive stepped roof; near-identical mass logic despite different base seed
curved bar family with lifted/notched frontage threshold and recursive curved roof; same sectional type with minor variation

required_next_relations: Add at least 6-7 new families that are materially different in section and void strategy, not just silhouette tweaks.
Prioritize courtyard, carve_void, split_wing, bridge, cross_mass, and bent_bar readings that create a public sequence of threshold -> hall -> court -> rooflight.
Introduce one civic-scale dominant gesture that is not a bar or box: for example a lifted hall over a court, a split-wing museum with bridge connection, or a cross-mass around a central void.
Ensure back-of-house remains visually subordinate to the public gallery mass in at least several candidates.
Avoid repeating the same stepped roof or curved roof profile across multiple cards; vary roof edge, void placement, and access relation to the west approach.
